title: How to Detox from Cocaine Safely
h1: How to Detox from Cocaine Safely
metaDescription: While it may seem easier to continue using than to face the effects of withdrawal, know that recovery is possible. So how do you detox from cocaine safely?

blocks.text: Cocaine is one of the most addictive illicit substances available, explaining why its abuse is so prevalent. If you or a loved one is struggling with cocaine use and addiction, it’s likely you are all too familiar with just how difficult it can be to stop once you have formed a dependence on it. While it may seem easier to continue using than to face the effects of withdrawal, know that recovery is possible and you deserve to live a life free from addiction. So how do you detox from cocaine safely?

Cocaine is an extremely powerful stimulant drug. Due to its highly-addictive nature, cocaine is classified as a Schedule II drug, meaning it has a high potential for abuse. However, it can be legally administered under the guidance of a doctor for some specific, legitimate medicinal uses. Derived from the coca plant, it is most commonly used as a recreational drug and stimulant.

While everyone’s experience with substance use and addiction is different, there are a number of symptoms that are recommended to look out for to determine whether you or someone you know has a cocaine addiction. The following signs that may be indicative of an addiction to cocaine:
● Physical symptoms, such as dilated pupils, nosebleeds, runny nose, or weight loss
● Changes in behavior, such as excitability, mood swings, becoming increasingly talkative, an increase in risky behaviors, a change in sleep patterns, or a change in appetite
● Social changes, such as an increased interest in social isolation or a loss of interest in people and activities that used to be enjoyed
● Evidence of cocaine use including white powder residue, or the presence of drug paraphernalia that may indicate recent drug use
How to Detox from Cocaine Safely

Once you have developed an addiction to cocaine, it can be difficult to stop. Cocaine addiction typically requires the intervention of a professional in order to safely detox and lower the likelihood of a relapse. A medically-assisted detox uses approved medication to help lessen the symptoms associated with withdrawal.

During a medically-supervised detox, you will have the support of round-the-clock medical professionals to ensure your safety. You will also benefit from the availability of therapists and counselors to cope with the emotional and psychological toll of cocaine detox and learn valuable skills to navigate post-detox life.
